symbols.name: \(Y_n(a)\)
symbols.def: Potential outcome under treatment state \(a\) on a causal extension.

symbols.name: \(\Gamma(\nu_0,\nu_1)\)
symbols.def: Set of couplings with marginals \(\nu_0\) and \(\nu_1\).

symbols.name: \(u_{a,n}\)
symbols.def: An optimal conditional quadratic Kantorovich dual potential for \(Q_{a,P_n}\).

symbols.name: \(J_n\)
symbols.def: Wavelet or sieve resolution satisfying \(2^{J_nD}\asymp n^{D/(2s+D)}\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat q_{a,-k,n}\)
symbols.def: Normalized fitted arm density satisfying \(\int_{\mathcal Y}\widehat q_{a,-k,n}(x,y)d\ell_{\mathcal Y}(y)=1\) for almost every \(x\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat V_{-k,n}\)
symbols.def: Plug-in conditional transport value from the fitted arm kernels.

symbols.name: \(r_{\phi,n}\)
symbols.def: Centered-potential rate derived from \(r_{q,n}\) by the proposed transport-stability argument.

symbols.name: \(r_{V,n}\)
symbols.def: Conditional-transport-value rate derived from \(r_{q,n}\) by the proposed transport-stability argument.

assumptions.condition: \(c\le q_{a,n}(x,y)\le C\) for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) and every \((x,y)\in\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\).

\(\mathcal X\) is the closure of a bounded connected Lipschitz domain in \(\mathbb R^{d_X}\), and \(\mathcal Y\) is the closure of a bounded connected uniformly convex \(C^2\) domain with nonempty interior in \(\mathbb R^{d_Y}\).

novel.justification: standard: connected-support first variation in Manole et al. (2024), Lemma 23, and standard global Brenier regularity on uniformly convex domains

assumptions.condition: With \(\mathfrak F\) denoting the feasible conditional-density class in \(def:coupled-fold-learners\), the quadratic Brenier potential \(b_{f_0,f_1,x}\) transporting \(f_0(x,\cdot)\) to \(f_1(x,\cdot)\) belongs to \(C^2(\mathcal Y)\) for every \(f_0,f_1\in\mathfrak F\) and almost every \(x\).

There exists a fixed constant \(m_{\mathrm{OT}}>0\) such that \(\nabla_y^2 b_{f_0,f_1,x}(y)\succeq m_{\mathrm{OT}}I_{d_Y}\) for every \(f_0,f_1\in\mathfrak F\), almost every \(x\), and every \(y\in\mathcal Y\).

standard.name: uniform A1-type lower Brenier curvature, manole2024plugin

assumptions.condition: There exists a fixed constant \(M_{\mathrm{OT}}<\infty\) such that \(\nabla_y^2 b_{f_0,f_1,x}(y)\preceq M_{\mathrm{OT}}I_{d_Y}\) for every \(f_0,f_1\in\mathfrak F\), almost every \(x\), and every \(y\in\mathcal Y\).

standard.name: uniform A1-type upper Brenier curvature, manole2024plugin

assumptions.condition: There exist fixed constants \(t_\pi,L_\pi>0\) such that \(\pi_n\in\Sigma(t_\pi,L_\pi;\mathcal X)\) and \(\varepsilon\le\pi_n(x)\le1-\varepsilon\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\), uniformly over \(\mathbf P\in\mathscr P\).

definitions.name: Smooth observed-law parent class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{P_n\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X\times\mathcal A\times\mathcal Y):P_n\text{ satisfies }ass:fixed-overlap,ass:compact-support,ass:bounded-arm-densities,ass:holder-arm-densities\}\). No lower bound is imposed on \(\sigma_n^2\); in particular, \(\sigma_n^2=0\) is permitted whenever the displayed member properties hold.

definitions.name: Normalized coupled foldwise transport learners
definitions.construction: Choose deterministic folds satisfying \(\max_{1\le k\le K}||I_{k,n}|-n/K|\le1\). Let \(\mathfrak F\) be the class of \(f\in\Sigma(s,L;\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y)\) such that \(c\le f\le C\) and \(\int_{\mathcal Y}f(x,y)d\ell_{\mathcal Y}(y)=1\) for almost every \(x\). Let \(\mathfrak F_{J_n}\) be a fixed finite \(L^\infty\)-net of \(\mathfrak F\), constructed by quantizing boundary-adapted tensor-wavelet coefficients through level \(J_n\), with mesh order \(2^{-J_ns}\) and logarithmic cardinality order \(2^{J_nD}\). Put \(N_{a,-k,n}=\sum_{j\notin I_{k,n}}1\{A_{j,n}=a\}\). If \(N_{a,-k,n}>0\), define \(\widehat q_{a,-k,n}\) as the lexicographically first minimizer over \(f\in\mathfrak F_{J_n}\) of \[\frac1{N_{a,-k,n}}\sum_{j\notin I_{k,n}:A_{j,n}=a}\left\{\int_{\mathcal Y}f(X_{j,n},y)^2d\ell_{\mathcal Y}(y)-2f(X_{j,n},Y_{j,n})\right\}.\] If \(N_{a,-k,n}=0\), use the first element of \(\mathfrak F_{J_n}\). For every \(k,n\), fix before observing the data a rule \(\mathsf A_{\pi,k,n}\) such that \((t,x)\mapsto\mathsf A_{\pi,k,n}(t)(x)\in(0,1)\) is jointly measurable for a training sample \(t\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\). Set \(\widehat\pi_{-k,n}=\mathsf A_{\pi,k,n}(\mathcal T_{-k,n})\), set \(\bar\pi_{-k,n}=\min\{1-\varepsilon,\max\{\varepsilon,\widehat\pi_{-k,n}\}\}\), and define \(\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}(B\mid x)=\int_B\widehat q_{a,-k,n}(x,y)d\ell_{\mathcal Y}(y)\). Select the conditional quadratic optimizer and a mutually \(c\)-conjugate dual pair measurably by the minimum-norm normalized tie-break, obtaining \(x\mapsto\widehat\gamma_{-k,n}(\cdot\mid x)\) and \(x\mapsto(\widehat u_{0,-k,n},\widehat u_{1,-k,n})\). Require dual feasibility, contact on \(\widehat\gamma_{-k,n}\), and \(\widehat V_{-k,n}(x)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int\widehat u_{a,-k,n}(x,y)\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}(dy\mid x)\). Finally set \(\widehat\phi_{a,-k,n}=\widehat u_{a,-k,n}-\int\widehat u_{a,-k,n}d\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}\), so its fitted-kernel mean is exactly zero.

definitions.name: Foldwise Hölder and propensity rate route
definitions.construction: Use the finite-net conditional-density empirical-risk minimizer in \(def:coupled-fold-learners\) with \(2^{J_nD}\asymp n^{D/(2s+D)}\). Define \(r_{q,n}=n^{-s/(2s+D)}\), \(r_{\phi,n}=r_{q,n}\), \(r_{V,n}=r_{q,n}\), \(r_{S,n}=r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n}\), and \(r_{\sigma,n}=r_{S,n}+n^{-1/2}\). The density rate is derived from approximation error \(2^{-J_ns}\), entropy \(\log|\mathfrak F_{J_n}|\lesssim2^{J_nD}\), and the empirical conditional-density loss. The transport-potential, value, signed quadratic-remainder, score, and variance rates are conclusions derived from the three all-feasible-pairs Brenier assumptions, dual contact, exact centering, and cross-fitting. No propensity smoothness or propensity rate is part of this density route.

definitions.name: Empirical score studentizer
definitions.construction: \(\widehat\sigma_n^2=n^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i\in I_{k,n}}[\widehat S_{-k,n}(O_{i,n})-\widehat\theta_n]^2\) and \(\widehat\sigma_n=(\widehat\sigma_n^2)^{1/2}\). In every studentized statistic in this core, define a quotient with denominator \(\widehat\sigma_n=0\) to equal zero.

definitions.name: Second-order conditional-transport handle
definitions.construction: Derive second conditional Brenier derivatives along local perturbations of \(Q_{0,P_n}\) and \(Q_{1,P_n}\), then combine their observed-data scores with a derivative-aware resampling rule.

definitions.name: Predetermined triangular law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathscr P=\{\mathbf P=(P_n)_{n\ge1}:\text{for every }n,\ O_{1,n},\ldots,O_{n,n}\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}P_n,\ P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}},\text{ and the support-geometry and three all-feasible-pairs conditional Brenier conditions hold}\}\). This complete-sequence class is fixed before observing any data and is not defined by coverage, asymptotic linearity, a remainder rate, or any conclusion of Theorem 2. Uniformity at row \(n\) means \(\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathscr P}P_n(\cdot)\).

definitions.name: Generic and primitive propensity-rate regimes
definitions.construction:
Fix before observing data a jointly measurable learner rule on every training complement and a deterministic sequence \(r_{\pi,n}\to0\). The generic maintained learner condition is
\[
\lim_{M\to\infty}\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathscr P}
P_n\!\left(\max_k\lVert\bar\pi_{-k,n}-\pi_n\rVert_{L^2(P_{X,n})}>Mr_{\pi,n}\right)=0.
\]
This is an estimator-side hypothesis and does not define membership in \(\mathscr P\). For the primitive H\"older regime, let \(\mathfrak G_{J}\) be a deterministic finite \(L^\infty\)-net of \(\{g\in\Sigma(t_\pi,L_\pi;\mathcal X):\varepsilon\le g\le1-\varepsilon\}\), with mesh \(2^{-Jt_\pi}\) and \(\log|\mathfrak G_J|\lesssim2^{Jd_X}\). On each training complement choose the lexicographically first minimizer of \(\sum_j(A_{j,n}-g(X_{j,n}))^2\) over \(g\in\mathfrak G_J\), and clip it to \([\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\), with \(2^{Jd_X}\asymp n^{d_X/(2t_\pi+d_X)}\).

statements.statement: Under \(ass:consistency\), \(ass:ignorability\), \(ass:fixed-overlap\), and \(ass:regular-support-geometry\), \(Q_{a,P_n}(\cdot\mid x)=\mu_{a,P_n}(\cdot\mid x)\) for \(P_{X,n}\)-almost every \(x\) and every \(a\in\mathcal A\). Thus \(\theta_n\) is the observed-law representation of the known sharp conditional-coupling lower endpoint on \(E[\lVert Y_n(1)-Y_n(0)\rVert_2^2]\). Over \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\), at laws satisfying \(ass:regular-support-geometry\), \(\psi_n\) is the canonical gradient of \(\theta_n\) in the nonparametric observed-data model and \(\sigma_n^2\) is its semiparametric efficiency bound.
statements.justification: The theorem separates the causal sharp lower endpoint from its observed-law representation and derives the inverse-propensity canonical gradient by a direct integrated-DQM calculation for every regular observed-data score.
statements.gap: Randomized marginal-sample transport limits do not supply the observational tangent decomposition, its covariate-composition term, or its inverse-propensity arm terms.
statements.consumer: It supplies the semiparametric efficiency benchmark and the influence function used by the cross-fitted one-step estimator.

statements.statement: Does there exist an honest, degeneracy-adaptive confidence procedure uniformly over the full frozen nonparametric conditional-transport class allowing \(\sigma_n\to0\), including exact equality, that is first-order efficient away from equality and correctly second-order calibrated at equality; and which uniform second-derivative, compactness, and spectral conditions are necessary and sufficient?
statements.justification: The broad adaptive question remains open after the exact degeneracy characterization and the route-specific spectral obstruction.
statements.gap: No construction here spans regular positive-variance sequences, arbitrary vanishing variance, and exact equality uniformly over the full parent.
statements.consumer: A solution would govern uncertainty reporting when the conditional-OT endpoint is nearly or exactly degenerate.
statements.proof_tex: The proved frontier theorem gives three sharp partial conclusions.  First, \(\sigma_n^2=0\) holds exactly at conditional equality, where \(\theta_n=0\), \(\psi_n=0\), and the oracle first-order pivot has Kolmogorov distance \(1/2\) from \(N(0,1)\).  Second, along the stated smooth equality paths the second derivative is twice the weighted Neumann energy.  Third, positive-variance sequences retain uniform first-order studentized normality whenever \(\sqrt n\,\delta_n/\sigma_n\to0\), \(\eta_n/\sigma_n^2\to0\), and \(\sqrt n\,\sigma_n\to\infty\).  The theorem additionally proves that an unregularized full-tangent spectral calibration is impossible at the displayed nonatomic equality law; only the broader regularized adaptive problem remains open.

statements.statement:
Under \(ass:holder-propensity\), use on every training complement the clipped finite-net least-squares learner specified in \(def:propensity-rate-regimes\). Then, uniformly over \(\mathbf P\in\mathscr P\),
\[
\max_{1\le k\le K}\lVert\bar\pi_{-k,n}-\pi_n\rVert_{L^2(P_{X,n})}
=O_{P_n}\!\left(n^{-t_\pi/(2t_\pi+d_X)}\right).
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a row \(n\) and fold \(k\), put \(m_k=n-|I_{k,n}|\), and suppress the row index. The deterministic fold-size condition with fixed \(K\) gives \(m_k\asymp n\). By \(ass:observed-iid\), the training observations are i.i.d.; write \(P\) and \(\mathbb P_{k,n}\) for their law and empirical measure. For \(f\in\mathfrak G_J\), let
\[
\ell_f(X,A)=(A-f(X))^2,\qquad \mathcal R(f)=P(\ell_f-\ell_\pi).
\]
Since \(E[A\mid X]=\pi(X)\),
\[
\mathcal R(f)=E[(f(X)-\pi(X))^2]=\lVert f-\pi\rVert_{L^2(P_X)}^2.
\]
Writing \(d_f=f-\pi\), boundedness gives
\[
\ell_f-\ell_\pi=d_f^2-2(A-\pi)d_f,\qquad |\ell_f-\ell_\pi|\le1,
\]
and, because \(E[(A-\pi)^2\mid X]=\pi(1-\pi)\le1/4\),
\[
E[(\ell_f-\ell_\pi)^2\mid X]\le2d_f^4+8E[(A-\pi)^2\mid X]d_f^2\le4d_f^2.
\]
Hence \(\operatorname{Var}(\ell_f-\ell_\pi)\le4\mathcal R(f)\). For the centered variable \(Z_f\), \(|Z_f|\le2\) and \(E|Z_f|^r\le2^{r-2}E[Z_f^2]\) for \(r\ge2\). Expanding the exponential series gives, for \(|t|<3/2\),
\[
\log E(e^{tZ_f})\le\frac{t^2E[Z_f^2]}{2(1-2|t|/3)}.
\]
Exponential Markov optimization and a union bound over the finite net therefore imply that, for every \(u>0\), with probability at least \(1-2e^{-u}\), simultaneously for all \(f\in\mathfrak G_J\),
\[
| (\mathbb P_{k,n}-P)(\ell_f-\ell_\pi)|\le\frac14\mathcal R(f)+C_0\frac{\log(2|\mathfrak G_J|)+u}{m_k}.
\]
By \(ass:holder-propensity\) and the net construction, some \(f^\circ\in\mathfrak G_J\) obeys
\[
\lVert f^\circ-\pi\rVert_\infty\le C_1 2^{-Jt_\pi},\qquad \mathcal R(f^\circ)\le C_1^22^{-2Jt_\pi},\qquad \log|\mathfrak G_J|\le C_2 2^{Jd_X}.
\]
If \(\widetilde\pi_{-k,n}\) is the empirical minimizer before clipping, its minimizing property and the simultaneous deviation bound at \(\widetilde\pi_{-k,n}\) and \(f^\circ\), followed by absorption of \(\mathcal R(\widetilde\pi_{-k,n})/4\), yield
\[
\mathcal R(\widetilde\pi_{-k,n})\le C_3\left(2^{-2Jt_\pi}+\frac{2^{Jd_X}+u}{m_k}\right).
\]
Projection onto \([\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\) is pointwise one-Lipschitz and fixes \(\pi\), so the same bound holds for \(\bar\pi_{-k,n}\). With \(2^{Jd_X}\asymp n^{d_X/(2t_\pi+d_X)}\), the deterministic terms have order \(n^{-2t_\pi/(2t_\pi+d_X)}\). Taking square roots and a union bound over fixed \(K\) proves, uniformly over \(\mathbf P\in\mathscr P\),
\[
\max_k\lVert\bar\pi_{-k,n}-\pi_n\rVert_{L^2(P_{X,n})}=O_{P_n}\!\left(n^{-t_\pi/(2t_\pi+d_X)}\right).
\]

statements.statement:
Under \(ass:holder-propensity\), the finite-net propensity learner and \(r_{q,n}=n^{-s/(2s+D)}\) satisfy the hypotheses of \(thm:regular-efficient-inference\) whenever
\[
s>\frac D2,\qquad \frac{t_\pi}{2t_\pi+d_X}+\frac{s}{2s+D}>\frac12.
\]
The second inequality is equivalent to \(t_\pi>Dd_X/(4s)\). If the propensity is known, take \(\bar\pi_{-k,n}=\pi_n\) and \(r_{\pi,n}=0\), so only \(s>D/2\) remains. If a correctly specified fixed-dimensional propensity learner has the uniform rate \(r_{\pi,n}=n^{-1/2}\), its product condition is automatic and again only \(s>D/2\) remains.
statements.justification: The proposition verifies the generic propensity premise with an explicit clipped finite-net learner on the structural H\"older-propensity subclass.
statements.gap: An estimator-side learner-rate premise alone does not identify a primitive law class on which the premise is attained.
statements.consumer: It gives the planning elbow \(t_\pi>Dd_X/(4s)\), with separate known- and parametric-propensity corollaries under their explicit uniform premises.

statements.statement:
Theorem 2 (conditional observational DML for the sharp COT endpoint). Fix the predetermined triangular law class \(\mathscr P\) in \(def:predetermined-triangular-law-class\). Use the normalized coupled learners in \(def:coupled-fold-learners\), the density route in \(def:foldwise-rate-route\), and a predetermined propensity learner satisfying the generic uniform rate condition in \(def:propensity-rate-regimes\) for a deterministic \(r_{\pi,n}\to0\). Suppose
\[
r_{q,n}^2=o(n^{-1/2}),\qquad r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n}=o(n^{-1/2}),\qquad r_{\pi,n}+r_{q,n}=o(1).
\]
Then, uniformly over \(\mathbf P\in\mathscr P\), the exact fold bias is
\[
\mathcal B_{k,n}=-E_{P_{X,n}}\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OT}}(Q,\widehat Q)
+E_{P_{X,n}}\sum_a\left(\frac{\pi_{a,n}}{\bar\pi_{a,-k,n}}-1\right)
\int\widehat\phi_{a,-k,n}\,d(Q_{a,P_n}-\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}),
\]
where \(\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OT}}\ge0\). Its two terms have orders \(O_{P_n}(r_{q,n}^2)\) and \(O_{P_n}(r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n})\). Moreover,
\[
\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_n(O_{i,n})+R_n,
\quad
R_n=O_{P_n}(r_{q,n}^2+r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n}+n^{-1/2}(r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n}))=o_{P_n}(n^{-1/2}),
\]
\[
\widehat\sigma_n^2-\sigma_n^2=O_{P_n}(r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n}+n^{-1/2})=o_{P_n}(1),
\]
and
\[
\sup_{\mathbf P\in\mathscr P}\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}
\left|P_n\!\left(\frac{\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n)}{\widehat\sigma_n}\le t\right)-\Phi(t)\right|\to0.
\]
Also \(\widehat\sigma_n/\sigma_n\to1\) uniformly in probability, \(\inf_{\mathbf P\in\mathscr P}P_n(\widehat\sigma_n>0)\to1\), and the two-sided Wald interval has uniform asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\). Its leading variance is the efficiency bound \(\sigma_n^2\).
statements.justification: On any predetermined \(\mathscr C\subseteq\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs}}_{\sigma_\star}\) satisfying the two estimator-side learner-rate premises, the theorem proves the exact fold bias, root-\(n\) asymptotic linearity, variance consistency, uniform studentized normality, efficiency attainment, and two-sided Wald coverage.
statements.gap: Lin--Gao--Blanchet--Glynn, arXiv:2506.00257v2, Theorem 6 gives an observational direct-COT finite-sample value-rate using two-fold cross-fitting and cellwise self-normalized propensity weights, but not an observed-data EIF, efficiency bound, uniform root-\(n\) studentization, variance consistency, or Wald coverage.  Their arXiv:2602.20681 Theorem 3.2 is a pointwise randomized-marginal smooth-COT limit theorem.
statements.consumer: It yields the variance-separated inferential guarantee for a 401(k) SIPP-style observational analysis when the causal, support, transport, nuisance-rate, and variance conditions are credible.

statements.statement:
For the constrained finite-net empirical-risk learners in \(def:coupled-fold-learners\), under i.i.d. sampling, fixed overlap, bounded arm densities, and Hölder arm densities,
\[\max_{k,a}\lVert\widehat q_{a,-k,n}-q_{a,n}\rVert_{L^2(P_{X,n}\otimes\ell_{\mathcal Y})}=O_{P_n}(2^{-J_ns}+\sqrt{2^{J_nD}/n})=O_{P_n}(n^{-s/(2s+D)})\]uniformly over \(\mathbf P\in\mathscr P\).

Uniformly over \(\mathbf P\in\mathscr P\), the conditional-density rate \(r_{q,n}\) implies
\[
\max_{k,a}\int W_2^2(\widehat Q_{a,-k,n},Q_{a,P_n})\,dP_{X,n}=O_{P_n}(r_{q,n}^2),
\]
\[
\max_{k,a}\lVert\widehat\phi_{a,-k,n}-\phi_{a,n}\rVert_{L^2(\nu_{a,n})}=O_{P_n}(r_{q,n}),\qquad
\max_k\lVert\widehat V_{-k,n}-V_n\rVert_{L^2(P_{X,n})}=O_{P_n}(r_{q,n}).
\]
With the fitted pair as base and the truth as perturbation,
\[
\widehat V_{-k,n}-V_n+\sum_a\int\widehat\phi_{a,-k,n}\,d(Q_{a,P_n}-\widehat Q_{a,-k,n})
=-\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OT}}(Q,\widehat Q)\le0,
\]
and its absolute value has order \(O_{P_n}(r_{q,n}^2)\).

If \(\mathcal Y\) is a bounded connected Lipschitz domain and \(f,g\in L^2(\mathcal Y)\) are probability densities satisfying \(f,g\ge c>0\), then
\[W_2^2(f\,d\ell_{\mathcal Y},g\,d\ell_{\mathcal Y})\le c^{-1}C_{\mathcal Y}^2\lVert f-g\rVert_{L^2(\ell_{\mathcal Y})}^2,\]
where \(C_{\mathcal Y}\) is a Poincar\'e constant of \(\mathcal Y\).

For any feasible base pair \(\overline P=(\overline P_0,\overline P_1)\) and perturbation pair \(P=(P_0,P_1)\), let \((\overline u_0,\overline u_1)\) be a quadratic dual optimizer at the base pair and define
\[
\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OT}}(P,\overline P)
=W_2^2(P_0,P_1)-W_2^2(\overline P_0,\overline P_1)
-\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int\overline u_a\,d(P_a-\overline P_a).
\]
Under the three uniform conditional Brenier assumptions, there is \(C_{\mathrm{OT}}<\infty\) such that
\[
0\le\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OT}}(P,\overline P)
\le C_{\mathrm{OT}}\{W_2(P_0,\overline P_0)+W_2(P_1,\overline P_1)\}^2.
\]
The assertion is unchanged by centering the base potentials.

Fix \(x\) in the common full-measure set from \(ass:uniform-conditional-brenier-smoothness\), \(ass:uniform-conditional-brenier-lower-curvature\), and \(ass:uniform-conditional-brenier-upper-curvature\). For feasible laws \(P,Q,\widehat P,\widehat Q\) on \(\mathcal Y\), let \(T=\nabla b\) be the Brenier map from \(P\) to \(Q\), and let \(\widehat\gamma\) be an optimal coupling of \(\widehat P\) and \(\widehat Q\). Then
\[
\frac1{M_{\mathrm{OT}}}\int\lVert\zeta-T(\xi)\rVert_2^2d\widehat\gamma(\xi,\zeta)
\le \frac1{m_{\mathrm{OT}}}W_2^2(Q,\widehat Q)+M_{\mathrm{OT}}W_2^2(P,\widehat P)
+2W_2(P,\widehat P)W_2(Q,\widehat Q).
\]
The analogous assertion holds for the reverse maps after swapping the marginals.

Assume the generic uniform propensity learner-rate condition in \(def:propensity-rate-regimes\). Under the conclusions of \(lem:conditional-transport-stability-rates\), uniformly over \(\mathbf P\in\mathscr P\),
\[\max_k\left|E_{P_{X,n}}\sum_a\left(\frac{\pi_{a,n}}{\bar\pi_{a,-k,n}}-1\right)\int\widehat\phi_{a,-k,n}\,d(Q_{a,P_n}-\widehat Q_{a,-k,n})\right|=O_{P_n}(r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n}),\]
and
\[\max_k\left\|\widehat S_{-k,n}-(\theta_n+\psi_n)\right\|_{L^2(P_n)}=O_{P_n}(r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n}).\]
statements.justification: This new lemma places the generic propensity learner premise exactly where it is used and proves both the propensity--density product bias and the full coupled-score \(L^2(P_n)\) rate.
statements.gap: The transport-only stability conclusions do not logically imply assignment-score rates without an independently stated propensity rate.
statements.consumer: It is the propensity-dependent bridge from transport stability to the cross-fit remainder and variance bounds.

statements.statement: There is a finite constant \(M_\psi\), depending only on \(\varepsilon\) and \(\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal Y)\), such that every \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\) satisfying \(ass:regular-support-geometry\) obeys \(E_{P_n}[\psi_n(O_{1,n})]=0\) and \(|\psi_n(O_{1,n})|\le M_\psi\) almost surely. Consequently, \(\sup_{n,P_n}E_{P_n}[|\psi_n|^r]\le M_\psi^r\) for every \(r\ge1\).

Under the hypotheses of \(lem:conditional-transport-stability-rates\) and \(lem:assignment-score-rates\), the exact conditional fold bias is
\[
\mathcal B_{k,n}=-E_{P_{X,n}}\mathscr D_{\mathrm{OT}}(Q,\widehat Q)
+E_{P_{X,n}}\sum_a\left(\frac{\pi_{a,n}}{\bar\pi_{a,-k,n}}-1\right)
\int\widehat\phi_{a,-k,n}\,d(Q_{a,P_n}-\widehat Q_{a,-k,n}).
\]
The first term is nonpositive and \(O_{P_n}(r_{q,n}^2)\); the second has no fixed sign and is \(O_{P_n}(r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n})\). Uniformly over \(\mathbf P\in\mathscr P\),
\[
\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_n(O_{i,n})
+O_{P_n}(r_{q,n}^2+r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n}+n^{-1/2}r_{S,n}),
\]
and \(\widehat\sigma_n^2-\sigma_n^2=O_{P_n}(r_{S,n}+n^{-1/2})\).

Suppose \(O_{1,n},\ldots,O_{n,n}\) are i.i.d., \(E[\psi_n]=0\), \(|\psi_n|\le M\), \(E[\psi_n^2]=\sigma_n^2\ge\sigma_\star^2\),
\[\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_n(O_{i,n})+o_{P_n}(n^{-1/2}),\qquad \widehat\sigma_n^2-\sigma_n^2=o_{P_n}(1),\]uniformly over \(\mathbf P\in\mathscr P\). Then the studentized statistic converges uniformly in Kolmogorov distance to \(N(0,1)\), \(\widehat\sigma_n/\sigma_n\to1\) uniformly, the denominator is positive with probability tending uniformly to one, and the associated two-sided Wald interval has uniform asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\).

Let \(Z_{1,n},\ldots,Z_{n,n}\) be i.i.d. within each row, with mean zero, variance \(v_n^2\ge v_\star^2>0\), and \(|Z_{i,n}|\le M\). Then \[\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\left|P\!\left(\frac{1}{v_n\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^nZ_{i,n}\le t\right)-\Phi(t)\right|\longrightarrow0\] uniformly over all row laws satisfying these two bounds.

Theorem (degeneracy frontier and obstruction to the unregularized full-tangent spectral route).  Let \(P_n\) be a row law of the variance-unrestricted parent \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vu}}\), equivalently \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\) satisfying \(ass:regular-support-geometry\) and the three all-feasible-pairs conditional Brenier conditions.  Then \(\sigma_n^2=0\) if and only if \(Q_{0,P_n}(\cdot\mid x)=Q_{1,P_n}(\cdot\mid x)\) for \(P_{X,n}\)-almost every \(x\).  At equality, \(\theta_n=0\), \(\psi_n=0\), and the oracle first-order Gaussian pivot has Kolmogorov distance \(1/2\) from \(N(0,1)\).  Along every smooth equality path described in \(\texttt{lem:equality-degeneracy-and-second-variation}\), the second directional derivative is the displayed weighted Neumann energy.  A centered Gaussian spectral calibration for a second-order Hessian exists in \(L^2\) exactly when its eigenvalues are square summable, and uniform finite-rank calibration requires a uniform square-summable tail.  The parent class does not imply this condition: whenever it contains the equality law in \(\texttt{lem:conditional-hessian-spectral-obstruction}\) with nonatomic \(P_X\), the conditional Hessian has an infinite-dimensional compression equal to a positive multiple of the identity and is neither compact nor Hilbert--Schmidt.  Consequently, the unregularized \(n\)-scale full-tangent spectral/Gaussian route named in \(\texttt{def:degeneracy-handle}\) cannot yield a uniformly tight equality calibration over \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vu}}\).  A positive theorem using that route must impose or construct covariate-direction regularization, a uniform Hilbert--Schmidt tail, and uniform estimation of the regularized Hessian.  On collections with \(\sigma_n>0\), the first-order studentized limit remains uniformly valid under the relative-rate conditions in \(\texttt{lem:vanishing-variance-studentization}\).  This is a route-specific negative result and does not rule out slower regularized or other derivative-aware confidence procedures; honest degeneracy-adaptive inference over the entire parent remains open.
statements.justification: The theorem characterizes exact first-order degeneracy, proves the positive relative-rate transition regime, and gives a concrete non-Hilbert--Schmidt obstruction to unregularized full-tangent equality calibration.
statements.gap: The obstruction is route-specific and does not prove impossibility of slower covariate-regularized or other derivative-aware confidence procedures.
statements.consumer: It explains why the variance-separated Wald theorem cannot be extended to equality by an unregularized spectral plug-in.

statements.statement:
Let \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\) satisfy \(\texttt{ass:regular-support-geometry}\). Then \(\sigma_n^2=0\) if and only if \(Q_{0,P_n}(\cdot\mid x)=Q_{1,P_n}(\cdot\mid x)\) for \(P_{X,n}\)-almost every \(x\). At such a law, \(\theta_n=0\), \(\psi_n=0\) almost surely, and the zero-denominator oracle first-order pivot is identically zero and has Kolmogorov distance \(1/2\) from \(N(0,1)\). Moreover, suppress the row index and consider a path that fixes \(P_X\) and \(\pi\), starts at conditional equality \(q_{0,0}=q_{1,0}=q\), and satisfies \(q_{a,t}=q+t h_a\), where \(\int_{\mathcal Y}h_a(x,y)d\ell_{\mathcal Y}(y)=0\). Suppose the path remains in \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\), the functions \(q,h_0,h_1\) are twice continuously differentiable in \(y\) with uniform bounds, and the mean-zero weighted Neumann solution \(w_x\) satisfies
\[
-\nabla_y\cdot\{q(x,y)\nabla_yw_x(y)\}=h_1(x,y)-h_0(x,y),\qquad q(x,y)\nabla_yw_x(y)\cdot\mathbf n(y)=0,
\]
with \(w_x\), \(\nabla_yw_x\), and \(\nabla_y^2w_x\) jointly measurable and uniformly bounded. Then
\[
\theta(P_t)=t^2\mathcal E+o(t^2),\qquad \mathcal E=\int_{\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y}q(x,y)\lVert\nabla_yw_x(y)\rVert_2^2d(P_X\otimes\ell_{\mathcal Y})(x,y),
\]
so the second directional derivative at equality is \(2\mathcal E\).

Let \(Z_1,Z_2,\ldots\) be independent \(N(0,1)\) variables and let \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\ldots\in\mathbb R\). The centered quadratic series \(\sum_{j\ge1}\lambda_j(Z_j^2-1)\) converges in \(L^2\) if and only if \(\sum_{j\ge1}\lambda_j^2<\infty\). If \(\lambda_j\ge0\), the uncentered series \(\sum_{j\ge1}\lambda_jZ_j^2\) converges in \(L^1\) if and only if \(\sum_{j\ge1}\lambda_j<\infty\). For a family \(\Lambda\) of square-summable sequences, common rank-\(J\) truncations approximate the centered series uniformly in \(L^2\) if and only if \(\lim_{J\to\infty}\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\sum_{j>J}\lambda_j^2=0\). If \(\lambda_j=\lambda_\circ>0\) for infinitely many \(j\), the centered partial sums have no weakly convergent subsequence.

Suppose the variance-unrestricted parent class contains an equality law \(P^\circ\) for which \(P_X^\circ\) is nonatomic, \(\pi^\circ(x)=1/2\), and \(q_0^\circ(x,y)=q_1^\circ(x,y)=q^\circ\) is a constant density lying in the interior of the frozen density bounds and H\"older ball. Then the equality Hessian of \(\theta\), viewed on the closure of regular observed-data scores in \(L_0^2(P^\circ)\), is not compact. More precisely, there is an infinite-dimensional closed score subspace \(\mathcal E\) and a constant \(\lambda_\circ>0\) such that the compression to \(\mathcal E\) of any bounded self-adjoint Riesz representative \(H^\circ\) of the second derivative equals \(\lambda_\circ I_{\mathcal E}\). Consequently \(H^\circ\) is neither compact nor Hilbert--Schmidt, and no unregularized square-summable spectral representation exists at this law.

Consider any collection of i.i.d. triangular sequences in the variance-unrestricted parent class with \(\sigma_n>0\), \(E[\psi_n]=0\), and \(|\psi_n|\le M_\psi\). Suppose, uniformly over that collection,
\[
\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_n(O_{i,n})+O_{P_n}(\delta_n),\qquad
\widehat\sigma_n^2-\sigma_n^2=O_{P_n}(\eta_n),
\]
where
\[
\frac{\sqrt n\,\delta_n}{\sigma_n}\to0,\qquad
\frac{\eta_n}{\sigma_n^2}\to0,\qquad
\sqrt n\,\sigma_n\to\infty
\]
uniformly. Then
\[
\sup_P\sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\left|P_n\!\left(\frac{\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n)}{\widehat\sigma_n}\le t\right)-\Phi(t)\right|\to0,
\]
\(\widehat\sigma_n/\sigma_n\to1\) uniformly in probability, and the associated Wald intervals have uniform asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\). For the frozen one-step decomposition one may take \(\delta_n=r_{q,n}^2+r_{\pi,n}r_{q,n}+n^{-1/2}(r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n})\) and \(\eta_n=r_{\pi,n}+2r_{q,n}+n^{-1/2}\), whenever its remainder conclusions hold uniformly on the sequence collection.

Let \(P_X\) be a probability law on \(\mathcal X\), and let \(Q_0,Q_1\) be jointly measurable probability kernels from \(\mathcal X\) to the compact metric space \(\mathcal Y\). Among all probability laws \(\widetilde P\) on \(\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y^2\) whose \(X\)-marginal is \(P_X\) and whose conditional \(Y_a\)-marginal given \(X=x\) is \(Q_a(\cdot\mid x)\),
\[
\inf_{\widetilde P}E_{\widetilde P}[\lVert Y_1-Y_0\rVert_2^2]=\int_{\mathcal X}W_2^2(Q_0(\cdot\mid x),Q_1(\cdot\mid x))dP_X(x).
\]
The infimum is attained by a jointly measurable conditional optimal-coupling kernel. If, in addition, \(A\mid X=x\) is drawn independently of \((Y_0,Y_1)\mid X=x\) with probabilities \(\pi_a(x)>0\), and \(Y=Y_A\), the resulting law is a causal extension satisfying consistency and conditional ignorability and having observed arm kernels \(Q_a\). Hence the displayed value is a sharp lower endpoint over causal extensions with these conditional marginals.
statements.proof_tex:
Disintegrate any admissible law as \(P_X(dx)\gamma_x(dy_0,dy_1)\). Its marginal restrictions say that \(\gamma_x\in\Gamma(Q_0(\cdot\mid x),Q_1(\cdot\mid x))\) for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\). Therefore, pointwise in \(x\),
\[
\int\lVert y_1-y_0\rVert_2^2d\gamma_x(y_0,y_1)\ge W_2^2(Q_0(\cdot\mid x),Q_1(\cdot\mid x)).
\]
Tonelli's theorem gives the lower bound after integration.

It remains to assemble pointwise optima measurably. Equip \(\mathcal P(\mathcal Y^2)\) with a metric generating weak convergence. This space is compact because \(\mathcal Y\) is compact. For each \(x\), the marginal constraints define a nonempty compact set \(\Gamma_x\), and continuity of the quadratic cost makes
\[
\mathcal C_x=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\gamma\in\Gamma_x}\int\lVert y_1-y_0\rVert_2^2d\gamma
\]
nonempty and compact. Its graph is measurable: the marginal equalities can be expressed using a fixed countable dense subset of \(C(\mathcal Y)\), every resulting kernel integral is measurable in \(x\), and the optimal-value equality is obtained as the decreasing limit of finite-partition transport linear programs with measurable coefficients. For completeness, take a countable dense sequence in \(\mathcal P(\mathcal Y^2)\). At stage \(m\), retain from the preceding compact section its intersection with the first closed ball of radius \(2^{-m}\) that meets it. Each first-index map is measurable because the relevant hitting events are measurable. The retained compact sections are nested, nonempty, and have diameters tending to zero; their unique limiting point \(\gamma_x^\star\) is measurable and belongs to \(\mathcal C_x\). Thus \(P_X(dx)\gamma_x^\star(dy_0,dy_1)\) attains the integrated pointwise value.

Finally draw \(A\), conditionally on \(X=x\), independently of \((Y_0,Y_1)\), with \(P(A=a\mid X=x)=\pi_a(x)\), and set \(Y=Y_A\). Then \((Y_0,Y_1)\perp A\mid X\), consistency holds, and positivity gives
\[
\mathcal L(Y\mid A=a,X=x)=\mathcal L(Y_a\mid X=x)=Q_a(\cdot\mid x).
\]
Hence the optimal conditional kernel supplies a compatible causal extension and proves sharpness.

statements.statement:
Let \(P\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\) satisfy \(ass:regular-support-geometry\), and let \(t\mapsto P_t\) be any regular dominated one-dimensional observed-data submodel through \(P=P_0\), with score \(h\in L_0^2(P)\), fixed support, and overlap in a neighborhood of zero. Define
\[
h_X(x)=E_P[h(O)\mid X=x],\qquad h_{Y,a}(x,y)=h(x,a,y)-E_P[h(O)\mid A=a,X=x].
\]
Then the observed-law functional \(\theta(P)=E_P[W_2^2(Q_{0,P}(\cdot\mid X),Q_{1,P}(\cdot\mid X))]\) is pathwise differentiable along the submodel and
\[
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\theta(P_t)\right|_{t=0}=E_P[(V(X)-\theta(P))h_X(X)]+\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}E_{P_X}\!\left[\int\phi_a(X,y)h_{Y,a}(X,y)Q_{a,P}(dy\mid X)\right].
\]
statements.proof_tex:
Suppress the row index and write \(L_t=dP_t/dP\).  Differentiability in quadratic mean means that, for some \(r_t\in L^2(P)\),
\[
\sqrt{L_t}=1+\frac t2h+r_t,\qquad \lVert r_t\rVert_{L^2(P)}=o(|t|). \tag{1}
\]
Squaring (1), using Cauchy--Schwarz, and using \(h\in L^2(P)\) give
\[
\left\lVert\frac{L_t-1}{t}-h\right\rVert_{L^1(P)}\longrightarrow0. \tag{2}
\]
Let \(\mathcal G_X=\sigma(X)\), \(\mathcal G_{XA}=\sigma(X,A)\), and put
\[
R_t=E_P[L_t\mid\mathcal G_X],\qquad M_t=E_P[L_t\mid\mathcal G_{XA}].
\]
Conditional expectation is an \(L^1\)-contraction, so (2) implies
\[
\left\lVert\frac{R_t-1}{t}-h_X\right\rVert_{L^1(P)}\to0,
\qquad
\left\lVert\frac{M_t-1}{t}-m\right\rVert_{L^1(P)}\to0, \tag{3}
\]
where \(m(X,A)=E_P[h\mid X,A]\).  The marginal likelihood ratio is \(R_t(X)=dP_{X,t}/dP_X(X)\); hence, with
\[
\rho_t(x)=\frac{dP_{X,t}}{dP_X}(x)-1,
\]
the first assertion in (3) is
\[
\left\lVert\frac{\rho_t}{t}-h_X\right\rVert_{L^1(P_X)}\to0. \tag{4}
\]

We next prove the conditional expansion rather than invoking a pointwise transport derivative.  For \(P\)-almost every \((x,a,y)\), disintegration gives
\[
1+\delta_{a,t}(x,y)
=\frac{dQ_{a,P_t}(\cdot\mid x)}{dQ_{a,P}(\cdot\mid x)}(y)
=\frac{L_t(x,a,y)}{M_t(x,a)}. \tag{5}
\]
Put \(m=E_P[h\mid\mathcal G_{XA}]\) and \(h_Y=h-m\).  We record the integrated conditional square-root expansion.  Conditional on \(\mathcal G_{XA}\), regard \(\sqrt{L_t}\) as a vector in the Hilbert space \(L^2(P(\cdot\mid X,A))\).  Its norm is \(\sqrt{M_t}\).  At the constant unit vector, the norm map has derivative \(v\mapsto E_P[v\mid X,A]\), while the normalization map \(v\mapsto v/\lVert v\rVert\) has derivative \(v\mapsto v-E_P[v\mid X,A]\).  To verify these derivatives in the integrated bundle, on the event that the conditional norm of \(t h/2+r_t\) is at most one half use the Hilbert-space Taylor identity with remainder bounded by a constant times the squared conditional norm.  Because \(r_t/t\to0\) in \(L^2(P)\), the conditional squared norm divided by \(t^2\) is uniformly integrable and the conditional norm converges to zero in probability.  Its squared-norm contribution on the complementary event is therefore \(o(t^2)\).  Truncating the conditional norm and then removing the truncation proves that both integrated squared remainders are \(o(t^2)\).  Applying the norm derivative to (1) gives
\[
\sqrt{M_t}=1+\frac t2m+a_t,
\qquad \lVert a_t\rVert_{L^2(P)}=o(|t|). \tag{5a}
\]
Write \(C_t=L_t/M_t\), with \(C_t=1\) on the null set where \(M_t=0\).  Applying the normalization derivative to (1), and using \(E_P[h_Y\mid X,A]=0\), yields the conditional Hilbert-fiber remainder
\[
\int\left(\sqrt{C_t}-1-\frac t2h_Y\right)^2dP=o(t^2). \tag{5b}
\]
This proves (5b) directly in the integrated Hilbert bundle, without imposing pointwise differentiability on the conditional kernels.

Let \(e_t=\sqrt{C_t}-1-th_Y/2\).  Since
\[
C_t-1-th_Y=2e_t+t h_Ye_t+e_t^2+\frac{t^2}{4}h_Y^2,
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz and (5b) give
\[
E_P[|C_t-1-th_Y|]=o(|t|). \tag{5c}
\]
Equations (5) and (5c) therefore imply
\[
E_P\!\left[\left|\frac{\delta_{A,t}(X,Y)}{t}-h_Y(X,A,Y)\right|\right]\to0. \tag{5d}
\]
Fixed overlap converts the arm-weighted integral in (5d) to the desired common-covariate integral: for every \(a\),
\[
\int_{\mathcal X}\!\int_{\mathcal Y}|g(x,y)|Q_{a,P}(dy\mid x)dP_X(x)
\le\varepsilon^{-1}E_P[1\{A=a\}|g(X,Y)|].
\]
Therefore
\[
\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int_{\mathcal X}
\left\lVert\frac{\delta_{a,t}(x,\cdot)}{t}-h_{Y,a}(x,\cdot)\right\rVert_{L^1(Q_{a,P}(\cdot\mid x))}dP_X(x)\to0. \tag{8}
\]
If
\[
Z_t(x)=\sum_a\left\lVert\frac{\delta_{a,t}(x,\cdot)}{t}\right\rVert_{L^1(Q_{a,P}(\cdot\mid x))},
\]
then the reverse triangle inequality and (8) show that \(Z_t\) converges in \(L^1(P_X)\) to \(\sum_a\lVert h_{Y,a}(x,\cdot)\rVert_{L^1(Q_{a,P})}\).  Thus \(\{Z_t:0<|t|<t_0\}\) is uniformly integrable.

Set \(V_t(x)=W_2^2(Q_{0,P_t}(\cdot\mid x),Q_{1,P_t}(\cdot\mid x))\) and \(V=V_0\).  On the compact outcome space, select base and perturbed mutually conjugate quadratic dual pairs jointly measurably as follows.  Restrict dual pairs to the common compact equicontinuous class supplied by the quadratic \(c\)-transform, impose the deterministic normalization \(\min_{y\in\mathcal Y}u_0(x,y)=0\), and fix a countable family of continuous linear functionals separating that class.  The feasible-optimal graph is Borel because dual feasibility is a countable collection of inequalities on dense subsets and every kernel integral is measurable in \(x\).  Successively retain the minimizers of the first, second, and later separating functionals.  At each step the hitting events of closed balls are measurable; the nested compact sections have diameters tending to zero, so their unique limiting point is a Borel selected optimizer.  Every selected potential has a common sup-norm bound \(B<\infty\).  At the base pair, positivity of the first marginal gives uniqueness of the Brenier map; equality of the gradients of two continuous optimizers on a full-measure set, connectedness of \(\mathcal Y\), the normalization, and mutual conjugacy then give uniqueness of the normalized dual pair.

Let \(u_{a,t}\) and \(u_a\) denote the selected perturbed and base potentials and put
\[
K_t(x)=\max_a\lVert u_{a,t}(x,\cdot)-u_a(x,\cdot)\rVert_\infty.
\]
Equation (8) implies integrated conditional total-variation convergence.  From any sequence \(t_m\to0\), choose a subsequence along which both conditional marginals converge in total variation for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\).  At such an \(x\), uniform boundedness and equicontinuity ensure that every further subsequence of the normalized perturbed dual pairs has a uniformly convergent subsubsequence.  Passing to the limit in dual feasibility and in the dual objective shows that its limit is a normalized base optimizer.  Base-pair uniqueness makes that limit \((u_0,u_1)\).  Hence \(K_t\to0\) in \(P_X\)-probability and \(0\le K_t\le2B\).  The uniform integrability of \(Z_t\) now gives
\[
\int K_t(x)Z_t(x)dP_X(x)\to0. \tag{9}
\]

Dual feasibility at the base and perturbed pairs supplies the full two-sided sandwich
\[
\sum_a\int u_a\,d(Q_{a,P_t}-Q_{a,P})
\le V_t-V
\le\sum_a\int u_{a,t}\,d(Q_{a,P_t}-Q_{a,P}). \tag{10}
\]
For either sign of \(t\), (10) and its sign-reversed version after division by a negative \(t\) imply
\[
\left|\frac{V_t(x)-V(x)}{t}-\sum_a\int u_a(x,y)\frac{\delta_{a,t}(x,y)}{t}Q_{a,P}(dy\mid x)\right|
\le K_t(x)Z_t(x). \tag{11}
\]
Integrating (11), using (8)--(9), and using boundedness of \(u_a\) gives
\[
\int\frac{V_t-V}{t}dP_X
\to\sum_aE_{P_X}\!\left[\int u_a(X,y)h_{Y,a}(X,y)Q_{a,P}(dy\mid X)\right]. \tag{12}
\]
Since each \(h_{Y,a}\) has conditional mean zero, \(u_a\) may be replaced in (12) by its centered version \(\phi_a\).

Finally, the changing-covariate-law decomposition is
\[
\theta(P_t)-\theta(P)
=\int(V_t-V)dP_X+\int V\rho_t\,dP_X+\int(V_t-V)\rho_t\,dP_X. \tag{13}
\]
By (4), the second term divided by \(t\) converges to \(E_P[V(X)h_X(X)]\).  The first term is handled by (12).  Equation (8) implies conditional total-variation convergence in \(P_X\)-probability; continuity of \(W_2\) on compact \(\mathcal Y\) therefore gives \(V_t-V\to0\) in \(P_X\)-probability, and \(|V_t-V|\le\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal Y)^2\).  Equation (4) makes \(\{\rho_t/t\}\) uniformly integrable, so
\[
\frac1t\int(V_t-V)\rho_t\,dP_X=o(1). \tag{14}
\]
Combining (12)--(14) and using \(E_P[h_X(X)]=0\) proves
\[
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\theta(P_t)\right|_{t=0}
=E_P[(V(X)-\theta(P))h_X(X)]
+\sum_aE_{P_X}\!\left[\int\phi_a(X,y)h_{Y,a}(X,y)Q_{a,P}(dy\mid X)\right].
\]

statements.statement:
Fix \(x\) and probability laws \(Q_0,Q_1\) on \(\mathcal Y\) whose densities are strictly positive, and let \((u_0,u_1)\) be a quadratic optimal dual pair. Suppose \(t\mapsto(Q_{0,t},Q_{1,t})\) is a two-sided path through \((Q_0,Q_1)\) such that, for \(a\in\mathcal A\),
\[
\left\lVert\frac{dQ_{a,t}/dQ_a-1}{t}-h_a\right\rVert_{L^1(Q_a)}\longrightarrow0,\qquad \int h_a\,dQ_a=0.
\]
Under \(ass:regular-support-geometry\),
\[
\left.\frac{d}{dt}W_2^2(Q_{0,t},Q_{1,t})\right|_{t=0}=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int u_ah_a\,dQ_a=\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int\phi_ah_a\,dQ_a,
\]
where \(\phi_a=u_a-\int u_a\,dQ_a\).
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(F(P_0,P_1)=W_2^2(P_0,P_1)\), \(\Delta_{a,t}=Q_{a,t}-Q_a\), and choose an optimal dual pair \((u_{0,t},u_{1,t})\) at the perturbed pair. Dual feasibility at the two pairs gives
\[
\sum_a\int u_a\,d\Delta_{a,t}\le F(Q_{0,t},Q_{1,t})-F(Q_0,Q_1)\le\sum_a\int u_{a,t}\,d\Delta_{a,t}. \tag{1}
\]
Quadratic conjugate potentials on compact \(\mathcal Y\) have a common Lipschitz constant depending only on \(\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal Y)\). Normalize every pair by fixing one potential at a fixed point. The normalized family is uniformly bounded and equicontinuous. Since \(\lVert Q_{a,t}-Q_a\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\to0\), every sequence \(t_m\to0\) has a subsequence along which the normalized perturbed potentials converge uniformly. Passing to the limit in dual feasibility and the dual objective shows that every such limit is optimal at \((Q_0,Q_1)\). The first marginal has a strictly positive density on connected \(\mathcal Y\); uniqueness of the quadratic Brenier map makes the gradients of any two optimal first potentials equal almost everywhere, and continuity plus connectedness then makes their difference constant. Conjugacy determines the other potential up to the opposite constant. The normalization removes this ambiguity. Consequently,
\[
\max_a\lVert u_{a,t}-u_a\rVert_\infty=o(1). \tag{2}
\]
The path hypothesis implies \(\lVert\Delta_{a,t}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}=O(|t|)\). Hence
\[
\left|\sum_a\int(u_{a,t}-u_a)d\Delta_{a,t}\right|\le\sum_a\lVert u_{a,t}-u_a\rVert_\infty\lVert\Delta_{a,t}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}=o(|t|).
\]
The sandwich (1) therefore gives
\[
F(Q_{0,t},Q_{1,t})-F(Q_0,Q_1)=\sum_a\int u_a\,d\Delta_{a,t}+o(|t|).
\]
Divide by \(t\) and use the asserted \(L^1\) derivatives. Since \(\int h_a\,dQ_a=0\), subtracting the armwise mean of \(u_a\) does not change the derivative, proving the centered formula.

sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment under consistency and conditional ignorability.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: On each training complement, a constrained jointly measurable conditional-density wavelet or sieve produces normalized arm densities bounded in \([c,C]\); a propensity is clipped to \([\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon]\). A deterministic measurable conditional-OT selection then generates the value, duals, and fitted-kernel-centered potentials from that same pair. Out-of-fold coupled scores define both estimator and empirical variance.

tldr:
Under consistency, conditional ignorability, and overlap, \(\theta_n=E_{P_n}[W_2^2(Q_{0,P_n}(\cdot\mid X_n),Q_{1,P_n}(\cdot\mid X_n))]\) is the sharp conditional-coupling lower endpoint for \(E[\lVert Y_n(1)-Y_n(0)\rVert_2^2]\).  Its observed-data canonical gradient is
\[
\psi_n(O)=V_n(X)-\theta_n+\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}}\frac{1\{A=a\}}{\pi_{a,n}(X)}\phi_{a,n}(X,Y),
\]
with efficiency bound \(\sigma_n^2=E_{P_n}[\psi_n^2]\).  For any predetermined \(\mathscr C\subseteq\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs}}_{\sigma_\star}\) on which the displayed density and propensity learner rates hold, the explicit cross-fitted coupled wavelet--Brenier one-step estimator \(\widehat\theta_n\) and studentizer \(\widehat\sigma_n\) satisfy
\[
\frac{\sqrt n(\widehat\theta_n-\theta_n)}{\widehat\sigma_n}\Rightarrow N(0,1)
\]
uniformly over \(\mathscr C\), attain the efficiency bound, and give two-sided Wald coverage tending uniformly to \(1-\alpha\).  The variance-unrestricted parent \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vu}}\) remains separate and permits equality.  At equality the first-order gradient vanishes; the proved spectral theorem obstructs only the unregularized \(n\)-scale full-tangent Gaussian calibration route.  A broadly honest degeneracy-adaptive procedure, including slower regularized or other derivative-aware constructions, remains open.

related_work: Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn's arXiv:2602.20681 Theorem 3.2 is the pointwise randomized-marginal comparator for smooth quadratic-COT asymptotic normality.  Their earlier covariate-aware work, arXiv:2502.01164, supplies identification and tightening motivation rather than the observed-data efficiency calculation.  Their arXiv:2506.00257v2/AISTATS Theorem 6 is an observational comparator: under unconfounded covariate-dependent assignment it uses two-fold cross-fitting, cellwise self-normalized inverse-propensity weights, and a discretized adapted-empirical direct COT value estimator; under its average weight-error condition with \(r=1/(d_Z+2\vee d_Y)\), it proves an expected absolute error bound of the form \(C^\dagger\gamma_{d_Y,d_Z}(n_0\wedge n_1)\).  That is a consistency/finite-sample value-rate result, not an observed-data EIF, efficiency, uniform root-\(n\) studentization, variance-consistency, or Wald-coverage result.  Ji, Lei, and Spector Theorem 3.5 establishes observational AIPW validity for fitted dual bounds under its two robustness regimes; their 401(k) SIPP analysis is the applied consumer motivating the present endpoint.  Manole and coauthors motivate the all-feasible-pairs Brenier regularity used for transport stability, while Newey--Robins and double/debiased machine-learning theory provide the general cross-fitting remainder template.  Sommerfeld--Munk-type transport limits and second-order directional or first-order-degenerate delta methods motivate equality calibration, but the present negative result is limited to the unregularized full-tangent spectral route.
interpretation: The causal object of interest is the lower endpoint \(\theta_n\), not the generally unidentified moment \(E[\lVert Y_n(1)-Y_n(0)\rVert_2^2]\) itself.  The canonical gradient contains a covariate-composition term \(V_n(X)-\theta_n\) and one inverse-propensity centered transport derivative for the realized arm.  On a predetermined variance-separated collection with valid nuisance-rate premises, \(\widehat\theta_n\) is asymptotically linear with this influence function, \(\widehat\sigma_n\) consistently estimates its efficiency-bound standard deviation, and the two-sided interval \([\widehat\theta_n\mathbin\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\widehat\sigma_n/\sqrt n]\) has uniform limiting coverage \(1-\alpha\).  In a 401(k) SIPP application, this interpretation requires credible ignorability, overlap, support and Brenier regularity, nuisance learning rates, and variance separation.
technical_internal_limitation: The regular theorem is intentionally uniform only over predetermined \(\mathscr C\subseteq\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs}}_{\sigma_\star}\).  The variance-unrestricted parent \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vu}}\) admits conditional equality, where \(\theta_n=0\), \(\psi_n=0\), and the zero-denominator first-order pivot has exact Kolmogorov distance \(1/2\) from \(N(0,1)\).  The second variation is a weighted Neumann energy, and at an admissible equality law with nonatomic \(P_X\) the full-tangent Hessian has an infinite-dimensional identity compression, so it is not Hilbert--Schmidt.  This rules out a uniformly tight unregularized \(n\)-scale Gaussian spectral calibration over the full parent.  It does not rule out slower covariate-regularized, derivative-aware, subsampling, or other honest adaptive procedures; constructing and validating such a procedure remains open.
honest_scope: Sharp causal identification uses consistency, conditional ignorability, fixed overlap, and measurable attainment of the conditional optimal coupling.  Canonical-gradient validity is pointwise at regular-support laws in the full nonparametric observed-data tangent space.  Uniform root-\(n\) inference additionally requires a predetermined collection inside \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs}}_{\sigma_\star}\), the stated support, density, and all-feasible-pairs Brenier conditions, and density and propensity learner rates imposed as estimator-side premises over that collection.  The primitive H\"older proposition verifies those rates only on \(\mathscr P^{\mathrm{vs,H}}_{\sigma_\star,t_\pi,L_\pi}\).  No claim is made under hidden confounding, overlap failure, nonsmooth or unbounded supports, or for a single honest procedure uniformly adaptive across all positive-variance sequences and equality.  The degeneracy theorem is a partial route obstruction, not a solution of that broad open problem.
